atlas_urls_assertion.note: Step (5) of `golden`: the three PRODUCED atlas sha256s are compared byte-for-byte against atlas-urls.json, which is in the receipt tier precisely so it survives the run dir.

inputs.note: Two tiers of pixels, and the asymmetry is the point. The three English atlases are here because their Steam URLs are third-party and can move -- but they are re-fetchable in principle. `delivered/` is LaMa inpainting output and has NO SECOND COPY ANYWHERE: not in git, not on R2, not in a release asset. If it is lost, this fixture cannot be reconstituted and v1's only end-to-end regression instrument is gone. `slices/` is deliberately NOT in the tier: it is a crop of these atlases and is therefore regenerable. `golden` binds to this manifest and refuses at EXIT 13 -- 'golden inputs missing or drifted', naming the first offending path -- rather than skipping, because a missing corpus is a restore job, not an environment difference.

masks_reference.claim_note: This is the reference side of 6 step 12's 're-derives Midwinter's masks from step 8's data and compares'. It asserts nothing about whether kz_mask SHOULD reproduce these bytes -- it only makes the comparison possible. A re-derivation that differs is a finding to adjudicate, not automatically a defect, because the legacy masks were built by build-masks.py and the catalogue has moved since.
masks_reference.shape_note: kz_mask.compare_manifests() reads reference["entries"] (kz_mask.py:1360) and keys on per-face `file` + `sha256`. The legacy document keys its array `masks[]`, so passing it directly leaves `ref` empty and reports all 88 derived faces as 'derived but absent from the reference'. Measured both ways on 2026-08-24 against a byte-identical mask set: the legacy file yields 88 findings, this one yields []. A single drifted digest yields exactly one finding.

copied_from.masks_reference: .am/midwinter-gala-korean/masks/manifest.json, RESHAPED -- see masks/manifest.json's own provenance{} block. The 88 PNGs it describes are the legacy build-masks.py masks as shipped on 2026-08-19, so it is a receipt for those bytes and not for anything kz_mask produced.
copied_from.text: .am/midwinter-gala-korean/card-text-ko.json -- the SHIPPED bytes, never a fresh render of data/text/midwinter-ko.py. The two differ on 71001 (see that file's KNOWN DIVERGENCE) and this is a byte-exact regression instrument, so rendering the generator would silently change the fixture. Its digest was checked against the value already recorded in `translate`'s and `check`'s binding{} and agrees with both.

provenance.copy_verified: sha256 compared source-vs-destination on all 91 files on 2026-08-24; every digest below is taken AT THE DESTINATION, so this manifest describes the tier rather than the run dir. The sources were COPIED, not moved: the Midwinter run dir is still referenced by the record and by atlas-urls.json.

seed.closure_note: THE SEEDED SET IS A CLOSURE, NOT A LIST, because a list is exactly what left `init` out. `golden` seeds the TRANSITIVE PREDECESSOR CLOSURE OF THE DRIVEN SET, MINUS THE DRIVEN SET. composite requires slice, mask AND erase; typeset requires composite AND check (<- translate <- terms); slice requires init. Independently, 3.2's gates{} marks init, mask and typeset required, and 3.6 makes gate.status == 'accepted' a `consumable` conjunct, so a fresh scratch run -- which writes `pending` gate stubs -- would stop at the first gate even with its predecessors satisfied. Stated as a closure the set is total by construction: adding a stage to the driven set recomputes it. `golden` refuses at EXIT 13 if this manifest does not cover every member of the closure, naming the missing stage.
seed.confinement_note: The seed is confined to the scratch run dir and is written by `golden` alone. No stage gains a seeding path, data/locks/midwinter.lock.json is never written by `golden`, the scratch dir is reached through `--run-dir` (argv, never scenario.json, so config_sha256 is untouched) and it is removed in a finally.

seed.note: `seed.manifest_sha256` and `seed.golden_run_id` are MINTED BY `golden` AT RUN TIME and are null here on purpose: the digest of this manifest cannot be a field inside the manifest it digests, and the run id does not exist until a run does. `golden` writes both into every report and gate it seeds, and `compute_consumable` carries the conjunct `seed is None or seed.golden_run_id == ctx.golden_run_id` -- so a seeded artifact is consumable to the stages of ITS OWN golden run and to nothing else: not to a real run in the same directory, not to a later golden, not to `plan`.

seed.labelling_note: Every seeded artifact is LABELLED as seeded, and the label is what stops it laundering the AI conjunct. A seeded `terms` or `translate` report must carry ai.used == true and ai.decide_outcome == 'proceed' or 3.6's last conjunct makes it non-consumable -- which means a seeded report is shaped exactly like one that really invoked claude, and nothing on disk could tell them apart. Hence seed{}. `--status` prints a seeded artifact as 'seeded (golden <id>)' rather than as a verdict.

check.files_note: Deliberately empty. `check` READS card-text-ko.json and binds its digest, but `translate` is what PRODUCES it, so it is materialised there. Listing it in both would have the seeder write one file twice, and a second writer is a second chance for the two copies to disagree.

erase.why_seeded: predecessor of `composite`. `erase` is the one seeded stage that is also REPLAYABLE: its output IS the fixture's delivered/, which this manifest already hashes. Driving the full nine-stage chain instead was the alternative and is rejected for v1 -- it puts two claude invocations (S1, S2) inside the regression instrument, which makes the instrument's result depend on a model version and makes it unrunnable offline. The coverage claim is narrower and is stated as such: `golden` proves the ARITHMETIC chain is byte-stable, not that the text chain is.

terms.why_seeded: predecessor of `translate`, which is a predecessor of `check`.

translate.files_note: `kz_typeset` reads <run_dir>/card-text-ko.json, so the seeder has to MATERIALISE it, not merely bind its digest. This is the same argument 5.8 makes for `init` -- 'init's seed carries its three data files as well as its report, because the driven stages read the FILES and not only the verdict' -- and it applies to every seeded stage whose consumer is a driven one. Without it a run that got past `mask` would refuse at `typeset` on a missing input.

NOTE the binding pins the SHIPPED card-text-ko.json, not a fresh render of the generator: the two differ on 71001 (see data/text/midwinter-ko.py's KNOWN DIVERGENCE) and it is the shipped bytes the atlases were typeset from.

tool_note: The REFERENCE interpreter triple, and it lives here because it is FIXTURE METADATA, not environment config. `golden` reads each driven stage's own tool{} block FROM ITS REPORT -- never by import -- and treats a null pil/numpy as 'this tier declares no opinion' rather than as a mismatch, since a stdlib-tier report cannot fill those fields without importing what it is forbidden to import. A mismatch is a SKIP at exit 75 with a named reason, never a pass: .am/fix-korean-grammar-defects/analyze.md records that running typeset-cards.py under 3.9.6 / Pillow 10.4.0 'would re-encode every PNG differently', and a golden fixture that quietly passed under a different Pillow would be worse than none. SCED-tools/scripts/requirements.txt pins Pillow==12.0.0 / numpy==2.4.2 with this fixture named as the reason.
